title: Canonical Schema Views for Activation Steering Under Tool-Schema Churn: A Negative Result

contributions.purpose: Save future researchers from pursuing schema canonicalization as a route to churn-invariant activation steering for tool-calling.
contributions.mechanism: DelexGate-ASA transforms tool schemas to generic placeholder identifiers (e.g. tool_0(arg_0_0, arg_0_1)) before ASA calibration and inference, remapping outputs back to real identifiers.
contributions.evaluation: On BFCL v3, DelexGate-ASA degrades clean-schema AST accuracy by 15.2 percentage points (from 81.4%/0.768 to 61.6%/0.616) while providing no robustness benefit under schema perturbations.
contributions.source_quote: First, we document a well-motivated approach (schema canonicalization for activation steering) that fails, saving future researchers from pursuing similar directions.

contributions.purpose: Explain why canonicalization fails for function-call accuracy.
contributions.mechanism: Failure analysis of argument-value mapping when parameter names are replaced by generic placeholders while descriptions are preserved.
contributions.evaluation: Experiments show LLMs cannot reliably map values to generic placeholders, attributing the 15.2pp accuracy drop to removal of semantic cues in parameter names.
contributions.source_quote: Second, we reveal that semantic information in parameter names is essential for function-call accuracy—LLMs cannot reliably map values to generic placeholders even when descriptions are preserved.

contributions.purpose: Establish whether ASA steering assets themselves need recalibration under schema churn.
contributions.mechanism: Transfer experiments reusing ASA steering vectors and probes trained on clean schemas against perturbed schemas, compared with recalibration.
contributions.evaluation: Recalibration provides no benefit over simple reuse, showing ASA's learned assets are inherently robust to lexical churn and degradation stems from base model sensitivity.
contributions.source_quote: Third, we show that ASA's learned assets are inherently robust to lexical churn: recalibration provides no benefit over simple reuse, indicating that degradation under churn stems from base model sensitivity rather than ASA asset drift.

self_declared_provenance.quote: We hypothesize that canonicalizing schemas to a stable placeholder vocabulary (e.g., replacing get_weather(location, unit) with tool_0(arg_0_0, arg_0_1)) before ASA processing could make the representation space invariant to surface-level identifier changes.
ASA (Wang et al., 2026) applies representation engineering to tool-calling... Our work investigates whether ASA's learned representations remain effective under schema churn.

We adapt the canonicalization idea to tool-calling activation steering, replacing tool and argument names with generic identifiers. However, our experiments reveal that this approach fails because LLMs rely on semantic information in parameter names for correct argument-value mapping.
However, no prior work has studied the robustness of activation steering methods to schema churn, which is the focus of our investigation.

notes: Explicit negative-result paper (declared in title and abstract): the proposed DelexGate-ASA fails decisively, degrading clean accuracy 15.2pp with no robustness benefit. All contributions are findings; contributions given as inline prose list, not bullets.
